article.title: Fi’s GPS-equipped dog trackers are on sale for 30 percent off
article.summary: If your dog or cat is prone to getting lost, or you frequently go on adventures together, you can save 30 percent on Fi pet trackers through October 25th when you enter coupon code SCARY at checkout. The sale includes several satellite-connected trackers,…
article.content: If your dog or cat is prone to getting lost, or you frequently go on adventures together, you can save 30 percent on Fi pet trackers through October 25th when you enter coupon code SCARY at checkout. The sale includes several satellite-connected trackers, including the Fi Ultra GPS we previously tested , which is down to $209.30 after the discount. That effectively brings it down to its original launch price. The IP68-rated Fi Ultra is fully waterproof, even in saltwater, and lasts up to five days, depending on how active your dog is. The accessory — which conveniently attaches to your dog’s collar or harness — uses a combination of LTE, GPS, and Starlink satellite coverage to track your dog’s current location and recent history, even in cellular dead zones; it can also send noise and vibration alerts to catch your canine’s attention. Fi Ultra dog tracker The Fi Ultra is the first dog tracker to combine T-Satellite with Starlink, GPS, and LTE connectivity to help you find your lost dog anywhere. Where to Buy: $299 $209.3 at Fi (with code SCARY) We spent time with the Fi Ultra earlier this year, testing it in a remote location in South Carolina. While the tracking was precise, the two- or three-minute update interval could be problematic for fast dogs, and it drained the battery quickly in Lost Mode (we barely got two days on a full charge). It’s also fairly sizable, making it a better fit for larger pups. Unsurprisingly, you’ll need an active subscription to use the Fi Ultra’s tracking features, though you’ll get a discount on your first term, with six-month, one-year, and two-year plans available that offer lower overall monthly rates. For example, a one-year plan is $99 for the first year, and $189 each year after. However, the plans only work in the United States and offer no satellite coverage in Alaska. Read our Fi Ultra review . Other deals to consider You can currently grab a physical copy of Kirby Air Riders for the Nintendo Switch 2 at Amazon for $48.99, a decent discount from its usual list price of $69.99. The colorful, fast-paced racing game offers surprising depth in terms of character and kart customization, with both cosmetic and functional upgrades to purchase and deploy over time. Read more . The JLab JBuds Talk USB-C microphone is on sale at Amazon for $24.99, where it usually fluctuates between $50 and $100, the full MSRP. A dedicated microphone can make a huge difference in audio quality over headphones or your laptop’s built-in mic. The Talk features four directional modes for different situations and a 96KHz/24-bit sample rate for high-quality recordings and voice clarity. Amazon is selling Lego’s Star Wars Grogu set for a discounted price of $103.99 ($26 off), which matches its lowest price to date. The 1,200-piece kit features Grogu in his beskar armor, with a satchel to carry his equipment (or snacks). You can also reattach his arms and facial features for different expressions, and a built-in lever lets you turn his head.
article.aiArticle:
Pet owners looking to keep closer tabs on adventurous cats and dogs can currently pick up discounted satellite-connected tracking hardware. According to **The Verge**, device maker Fi has launched a **30 percent** discount across its lineup of location-monitoring collars. 

The promotional pricing is available for a limited window, running only until **October 25th**. Buyers must enter the coupon code **SCARY** during the online checkout process to receive the price reduction, the report states. 

## Tracking Tech and Background

The hardware markdown applies to multiple satellite-enabled models designed to locate roaming animals. These devices have grown increasingly popular among owners who travel with their pets or manage independent animals that frequently wander off. 

While companion animal wearables have evolved significantly in recent years, hardware costs and recurring subscription fees often present a barrier for everyday consumers. Similar retail discounts frequently arrive alongside broader consumer electronics shifts, such as when [PC shipments dropped over 20 percent in Q3 due to RAM price hikes](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/pc-shipments-dropped-over-percent-in-q-due-to-ram-price-hikes), forcing manufacturers to adjust promotional strategies across multiple tech sectors.

## Why This Matters

This discount lowers the financial barrier for pet safety tools, which directly impacts owners living in rural areas or households with high-escape-risk animals. Reliable satellite location tracking can mean the difference between a quick recovery and a lost pet, though ongoing subscription costs required by these ecosystems remain a long-term financial consideration for buyers. 

What to watch: Future holiday sales cycles will likely determine whether competitor brands respond with matching discounts before the end of the fourth quarter. 

Sources: [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/1017196/fi-ultra-gps-dog-tracker-kirby-air-riders-deal-sale)
